messages:
Maya (Platform): Heads-up — planning a canary rollout for model-v3 at 14:00 PT. I want to lock down the rollout guardset: latency SLO checks, error-rate checks, and a token-cost delta threshold that can auto-pause. Any objections?
Sam (Runtime): +1 on latency + error. For cost: do we mean absolute tokens/sec or delta vs baseline traffic?
Maya (Platform): Delta vs baseline. We saw a quantized variant spike token usage by ~40% in load tests last week. Want a guard to catch regressions like that.
Li Chen: Important: telemetry lag. Prometheus pulls are at 30s, but our observable aggregation adds ~45s. If guards use a 1m window they might miss fast regressions or false-trigger on noise.
Nora: Can we use a two-tier window? fast short window for big deviations (30s) but require sustained breach for automated rollback (5m)? Also consider a soft-pause that routes to fallback model with a warning.
Sam (Runtime): Agreed. Implementation note: control-plane should evaluate gates (fast, near-real-time) and emit decisions; console shows history and lets SRE override. Debating whether evaluation lives in routing proxy or control-plane. Latency SLO check needs raw RT metrics from edge to be reliable.
Maya (Platform): I prefer control-plane eval with a small agent near proxies that feeds high-res metrics. Keeps routing simple and lets us centralize policy.
Li Chen: If we centralize, we need bounded decision latency. Otherwise auto-pause defeats purpose. Also must avoid flapping — include cooldown after pause.
Sam (Runtime): Cooldown makes sense. Suggested default policy:
```json
{
  "guards": [
    {"name":"latency_p50","type":"latency","threshold_ms":120,"window_s":30,"action":"pause-if-exceeds","sustain_s":90},
    {"name":"error_rate","type":"error_rate","threshold_pct":0.8,"window_s":60,"action":"pause-if-exceeds","sustain_s":120},
    {"name":"token_cost_delta","type":"token_cost_delta","threshold_pct":25,"window_s":120,"action":"pause-if-exceeds","sustain_s":300}
  ],
  "pause_cooldown_s":600,
  "on_pause":"route-to-fallback",
  "alert_policy":"page-on-pause"
}
```
Nora: That config looks reasonable as a starting point. Question: "pause-if-exceeds" vs "rollback" — I'd prefer pause (traffic freeze) and route to fallback model. Rollback is heavier and might cause data churn on A/B metrics.
Maya (Platform): Agreed. Pause + route to stable model is safer. We should add an optional auto-notify to the rollout thread in Slack. rollout-bot: I can post when a guard triggers and include a one-click pause/unpause button.
rollout-bot: @Maya (Platform) I can wire a message with actions. Need the action endpoints (control-plane URLs) and least-privileged token. :robot_face:
Li Chen: Also need to surface the metrics used for decision in the UI: baseline, current, pct-delta, and sample count. Without sample count SREs will get lots of noisy pages.
Sam (Runtime): Implementation detail: when traffic split <5% we should use an amplification factor on significance thresholds (i.e., be more tolerant) since small buckets are noisy. Also maybe require synthetic traffic injection for splits below 2% so we can exercise the model deterministically.
Maya (Platform): Good point. Let's add a split-aware policy. UX idea: console should show a suggested guard preset when user selects a canary % with rationale: "small canary -> relaxed thresholds or synthetic traffic".
Nora: Ops ask: what about cost SLOs? Some customers care more about token spend than latency. We should allow guard profiles per-customer that prioritize cost over latency (e.g., auto-pause on >15% token-cost delta even if latency ok).
Maya (Platform): We need per-tenant guard overrides. Add feature request to console: guard templates + per-route overrides + JSON advanced mode.
DevOps Bot: Test plan reminder: run chaos tests with synthetic spikes and long-tail latency for 3 variants and validate pause/unpause workflow. @eng-sre please coordinate.
Sam (Runtime): One more internal API debate: Do we expose guard evaluation outcomes as a single boolean "allow_traffic" in the SDK, or expose the full decision set (list of gates with reasons)? I vote full decision set — better for debugging.
Li Chen: Full set + timestamps. Also record raw metric snapshots to trace events.
Maya (Platform): Agreed. For SLO auditing we store "decision blob" with gate ids and metric snapshots for 30 days.
Nora: TL;DR action items: 1) Sam + Li to prototype control-plane eval agent and split-aware thresholds. 2) Maya + Nora to design console presets & Slack actions. 3) rollout-bot to wire notifications. 4) Eng-sre to run chaos plan. I'll post a tentative RFC later today. :thumbsup:
